judgments.reasoning_cat1: A binary election with an express default if no written election is made; the drafting anticipates its own gap. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subparagraphs (b), (c) and (d) work out both branches consistently, and Annex VII paragraph 1 applies a similar per-Fund logic. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four enumerated consequences of the separate-Principals election, each specific, with a parenthetical allowing a Principal-by-Principal margin alternative. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It modifies how Paragraph 4 margining and Paragraph 11 remedies operate and implicitly qualifies Paragraph 12's single-agreement netting, though it says so expressly by deeming separate Agreements. Workable together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The single-Principal branch is stated in three concrete consequences, qualified only by "any greater requirement imposed by applicable law." Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It aggregates margin across Principals, which sits against Annex VII paragraph 1(a)'s insistence on per-Fund application and 4(d)'s ERISA carve-out; those are expressly reconciled by their own "notwithstanding" language. No live conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A "notwithstanding any other provision" override with a single, precisely stated consequence for ERISA plans. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overrides 4(a)'s election and 4(c)'s aggregation in ERISA cases and complements Paragraph 18's plan-asset regime. Expressly reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deeming machinery is elaborate and turns on constructions "subject to the provisions of this Annex IV," leaving how far Agent is bound as a "party" to be worked out. The parenthetical making an Act of Insolvency of Agent an Event of Default by Seller or Buyer is a strong deeming rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Deeming Agent a "party" with a Principal's Event of Default consequences pulls against Annex IV paragraph 3, which says Agent's obligations do not include a guarantee of its Principals' performance and bars set-off against Agent's own transactions. The two can be reconciled only by reading paragraph 3 as the controlling qualification, which paragraph 5 acknowledges.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Forward Exposure" is "the amount of loss a party would incur upon canceling ... and entering into a replacement transaction, determined in accordance with market practice or as otherwise agreed" — a hypothetical loss measured by an unfixed external standard. That is a nameable vagueness at the heart of the annex.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The chain of definitions feeds Annex V paragraph 2's margining and depends on the Agreement's "Market Value," inheriting whatever indeterminacy that carries. Otherwise consistent with Paragraph 4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger rests on Net Unsecured Forward Exposure and on collateral "reasonably acceptable" to the calling party, both evaluative but structurally parallel to Paragraph 4(a). Moderately soft.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It states that these rights are "in addition to" Paragraph 4(a) and (b), so overlapping calls on the same Transaction are contemplated rather than prohibited. The interaction with Paragraph 4 is expressly addressed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure enabling threshold provision requiring further agreement. Nothing operative to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No such agreement appears in Annex I, so the option was never exercised. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enabling election for per-Transaction calculation, mirroring Paragraph 4(f). Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Paragraph 4(f) and Annex IV paragraph 4(b)(iii). No clash.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two enabling alternatives for initial and minimum transfer amounts, each requiring an agreed figure. Nothing indeterminate in the wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It relies on the Margin Notice Deadline, which the parties never fixed, so the timing runs on the 2(i) market-practice default. A dependency rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A same-day/next-day timing rule identical in structure to Paragraph 4(c). Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on the undefined Margin Notice Deadline and mirrors Paragraph 4(c) consistently. No inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A return obligation on settlement subject to a clear proviso preventing the creation of exposure. Precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coordinates with Annex V paragraph 2(a) and with the Purchase Date definition in Paragraph 2(n). Coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision uses "Pledgor (as defined below)" and "Pledgee (as defined below)" although those terms are first defined in the following paragraph — a forward reference that is untidy but recoverable. The substitution mechanic itself is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels Paragraph 9(a) for Forward Collateral without displacing it, and no annex contradicts it. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad pledge and set-off grant covering Forward Collateral "and any other cash, Securities or property" transferred or due — the sweep-in of anything "due from Pledgee to Pledgor" is wide but expressly stated. Little hidden ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expressly "[i]n addition to the rights granted ... under Paragraph 6," which itself only creates a deemed pledge if Transactions are recharacterised as loans; the two grants operate at different levels. No contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An expansive rehypothecation right with a proviso preserving return obligations; the drafting is explicit about the excess amounts and longer periods it permits. Clear if aggressive.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors Paragraph 8's treatment of Purchased Securities and preserves the transfer duties under Annex V paragraph 2 and Paragraph 11. Coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An additional Event of Default triggered only after one business day's notice, covering "any covenant or obligation" under the annex. Broad but plainly worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its notice requirement differs from Paragraph 11(iii)'s immediate default for margin failures, the same asymmetry seen in Annex III paragraph 8(a). Different triggers, not contradictory ones.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It repeats the same self-judging standards as Paragraph 11(d) — "commercially reasonable manner," prices the nondefaulting party "may reasonably deem satisfactory," "sole discretion" pricing sources — and again stipulates that all Forward Collateral "are instruments traded in a recognized market." Those stipulations are contestable in the same way.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expressly additional to Paragraphs 11 and 12 and keys off Paragraph 11(a)'s option, but its recognized-market stipulation cuts against its own commercially-reasonable alternative and against Paragraph 2(j)'s agreed-source valuation. The tension parallels the one in the main body.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line non-waiver saving clause mirroring Paragraph 17's last sentence. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly operates "[w]ithout limitation of the provisions of Paragraph 17" and matches it. Coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A scope recital identifying the annex, the date and the parties; wholly definitional. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is made applicable by Annex I paragraph 1 even though no Buy/Sell Back Transactions are evidenced, which is a checkbox oddity rather than an inconsistency. The substantive precedence rule sits in paragraph 1 of the annex.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A blunt precedence rule using the undefined trigger "any conflict"; the wording itself is short and plain. Limited intrinsic ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It makes Annex VI prevail over "any other term of the Agreement," while Annex I paragraph 2 makes Annex I govern over the Agreement and Annex VII claims the same primacy — three unranked precedence clauses with no tie-breaker. Where Annex I paragraph 3 and Annex VI paragraph 9 give opposite Income rules, this circularity actually bites.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mandatory classification requirement stated in one line; the consequence of failing to classify is not addressed. That silence is a gap rather than an ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires identification "in the relevant Confirmation," yet Paragraph 3(a) permits oral agreement and Paragraph 3(b) leaves who delivers a Confirmation to agreement, so an unclassified trade's status is unresolved. A modest coherence question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A permissive documentation rule allowing one or two Confirmations. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits comfortably with Paragraph 3(b) and Annex VI paragraph 5's Pricing Rate recording requirement. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The two sentences describe overlapping accrual periods, the first running to the date of calculation and the second to the next Income payment or maturity date, which is confusing on its face. The intent is recoverable but the drafting is doubled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It uses the Agreement's "Income" definition and feeds Annex VI paragraph 7's Purchase Price and Sell Back Price adjustments. Consistent in use.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise daily-accrual formula parallel to Paragraph 2(k), with an express opt-out from the 360-day convention. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds the Sell Back Price formula in 4(c)(ii) and is consistent with Paragraph 2(k)'s Price Differential. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-limb definition, the second an algebraic formula with defined variables; the OCR renders "the product of the formula (P + D) - (IR + C)" although the expression is a difference, not a product. That mismatch between the words and the symbols is a mechanical defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is invoked "for the purposes of the application of Paragraph 4 or Paragraph 11 of the Agreement" and is reinforced by Annex VI paragraphs 10 and 11's construction directives. Coherent with those.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short mandatory obligations about agreeing and recording terms. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supplements Paragraph 3(b)'s Confirmation contents without contradiction. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A termination mechanic distinguishing the originally agreed Repurchase Date from any other case, each routed to a specific definition. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels Paragraph 3(c) for Buy/Sell Back Transactions and coordinates with Paragraph 2(q). No conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The whole rule is subject to "except to the extent contrary to market practice with respect to the Securities," an unfixed external standard that switches the parties into an entirely different formula. That switch turns on a contestable factual standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It rewrites the 4(c)(ii) formula and interacts with 4(a) Accrued Interest and Paragraph 2(o)'s Purchase Price; the substitution is stated expressly. Reconcilable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It presupposes a repricing regime ("at the time of repricing") that the Agreement nowhere establishes, and the opt-out is located in an Annex I that says nothing about repricing. The unanchored reference is a real gap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex I contains no Buy/Sell Back repricing election, so the default is an obligation to agree terms at an event the instrument never defines. That incompleteness is confined to the Buy/Sell Back annex.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short sentences: Paragraph 5 is disapplied and Income flows from Seller to Buyer instead. The words themselves are plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It squarely reverses Paragraph 5 and cannot be reconciled with Annex I paragraph 3, which mandates that Buyer transfer Income to Seller under Paragraph 5(i) "in any Transaction hereunder" — and Annex I paragraph 2 and Annex VI paragraph 1 each claim precedence over the other. That is a genuine, unranked conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A sweeping construction directive rewriting a defined term "throughout the Agreement" as "Repurchase Price or the Sell Back Price, as the case may be," with no indication of how to tell which case is which. The phrase "as the case may be" carries all the work.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Applied literally it alters Paragraphs 2(c), 2(s), 4(e), 11(b), 11(e) and 11(f) even for ordinary Repurchase Transactions, which the parties presumably did not intend. Paragraph 11 also gets a separate, narrower directive in Annex VI paragraph 11, raising the question why both were needed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence opens "In 11 of the Agreement," omitting the word "Paragraph," and duplicates the broader directive in the immediately preceding paragraph. Both the omission and the redundancy are visible on the face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with Annex VI paragraph 10, which already covers every reference throughout the Agreement including Paragraph 11, leaving the narrower rule with no independent work. A redundancy rather than a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recital defines the parties as Barclays and "each investment company identified on Schedule VII.A," and embeds a precedence rule using the undefined trigger "any conflict." The definitional chain depends on a schedule that was left blank.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: As adopted by Annex I paragraph 1, this annex purports to substitute unnamed Funds for Thornburg as counterparty and to prevail over "any other term of the Agreement," competing with Annex I paragraph 2 and Annex VI paragraph 1 for primacy. Reading it into a two-party principal deal produces genuine incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The per-Fund ring-fencing is expressed clearly with three specific illustrations. Nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It disapplies Paragraph 12's single-agreement and set-off provisions across Funds and overrides Paragraph 4 aggregation, all expressly; but it does so in an annex made applicable to a deal with no identified Funds. The override is stated, so the incoherence is one of applicability.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The percentage is left blank ("equal to at least _%"), and the second sentence, addressed to a Fund acting as Seller, still speaks only of the Buyer's Margin Percentage — a blank plus an apparent drafting slip in the same short paragraph. Both defects are visible on the face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overrides Paragraph 2(d)'s and 2(t)'s default margin-percentage formulas with a 100% floor for any Fund Transaction, and Annex I paragraph 1 makes the annex applicable even though Schedule VII.A identifies no Fund. The blank and the floor cannot both be given effect coherently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short obligations to issue Confirmations and transfer notices, qualified only by "[u]nless otherwise agreed" and "promptly." Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It allocates the Paragraph 3(b) Confirmation duty to Counterparty, which Paragraph 3(b) leaves to agreement — a supplement rather than a conflict. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A representation about financial information delivered, with the applicable category keyed to specific SEC and Investment Company Act rules. Precise in its references.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels Paragraph 18(b)-(c)'s financial-statement regime for plan Transactions without contradicting it, and its breach would feed Paragraph 11(vi). Coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A concrete delivery mechanic routed through a designated Custodian, with a special case where the transferor is itself the Custodian. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on a Custodian "designated for such Fund in Schedule VII.A," and that schedule is entirely blank, so the mechanic has no referent; it also sits alongside Paragraph 8's segregation rule. The dependency on an unfilled schedule is the weak point.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision consists of an introductory sentence followed by empty "Name of Fund" and "Custodian" columns, so it identifies nothing. An unexecuted schedule is a defect visible on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex VII, Annex VII paragraph 5 and Annex VII paragraph 2 all depend on this schedule, and Annex I paragraph 1 nonetheless lists it as forming part of the Agreement. Making an empty schedule operative is a coherence problem for the instrument as a whole.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is an unfilled template: "[insert appropriate language limiting liability of trustees, officers and others]." There is no operative text at all, which is the plainest form of mechanical defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is made part of the Agreement by Annex I paragraph 1 even though no Fund, still less a business trust, is identified on Schedule VII.A, so the condition for its operation can never be met. Its emptiness leaves nothing to conflict with elsewhere.
